name: Initialize Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind scaffold
w: There is no code in the repo yet. Nothing else in this roadmap can start until a runnable skeleton exists with strict TypeScript and Tailwind already wired, so later tasks add features instead of re-arguing setup.
ac: npm run dev serves the default page with no console errors
TypeScript strict mode enabled and npx tsc --noEmit passes
A test element proves Tailwind classes are compiled
npm run lint runs clean
Node pinned to 24 LTS in package.json engines and .nvmrc, matching the Vercel runtime
out: No database, no auth, no UI design, no deployment.
f: package.json, .nvmrc, tsconfig.json, postcss.config.mjs, src/app/globals.css, src/app/layout.tsx, src/app/page.tsx

name: Initialize Git repository and connect GitHub remote
w: Version control and an off-machine backup must exist before feature code is written, otherwise early refactors are unrecoverable. The GitHub CLI is already installed on this machine.
ac: .git initialised on branch main
.gitignore excludes node_modules, .next and all .env files
Initial commit pushed to a private GitHub remote
git status is clean after the first push
out: No CI workflow (covered by EP-09) and no branch protection rules yet.

name: Provision Supabase project and wire environment variables
w: The app needs a Supabase project and working credentials before any schema or query work. Keeping secrets out of the repo from the very first commit prevents the most common and most expensive data leak in Supabase projects.
ac: Hosted Supabase project created; it serves as the staging environment (E9-T4), while day-to-day development runs on local Supabase (E1-T7)
.env.local holds NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (the newer publishable and secret keys can be used in the same variables)
.env.example committed with variable names and empty values only
Startup validation fails loudly when a required variable is missing
The service-role key is imported only from server-side modules
out: No tables, no policies and no storage buckets in this task.

name: Create Supabase client helpers for browser and server
w: Supabase needs two deliberately separate clients: a browser client for public reads and a server client that can read the auth cookies. Getting this boundary wrong leaks the service-role key into the client bundle, so it is done early and on purpose.
ac: Browser client exported from src/lib/supabase/client.ts
Server client exported from src/lib/supabase/server.ts and reads the session from cookies
A server component can render the current session
Grep of the production build output shows the service-role key is absent from client chunks
out: No auth UI yet; that is EP-02.

name: Define core domain TypeScript types
w: Shared types stop the same entity from being described differently in the database, the server actions and the UI. Defining them once now prevents silent drift as the schema grows.
ac: Types exist for Hostel, Room, Bed, Resident, Allocation, FeeStructure, Invoice, Payment and Profile
Insert and update variants exist where they differ from the read model
Numeric money fields are typed as integers with a documented unit
The project compiles with strict mode enabled
Derived state (bed occupied, allocation live, invoice paid/partial/overdue) is modelled as computed values, never as stored columns
out: Generated Supabase database types arrive with E1-T7 (npm run db:types) for typed queries; this task defines the hand-written domain model used by business logic.

name: Build app shell with navigation and shared UI primitives
w: Every feature page needs the same shell and the same handful of controls. Building them once keeps the product visually consistent and lets later tasks focus on behaviour rather than styling.
ac: Responsive shell with navigation that is usable at 375px width
Primitives exist: Button, Input, Select, Checkbox, Modal, Table, Badge and EmptyState
Standard loading and error states defined for any page
A route inside the (app) group renders inside the shell
Focus states are visible on every interactive control
out: No marketing site, landing page or dark mode.

name: Establish SQL migration workflow with Supabase CLI
w: Schema changes must be repeatable and reviewable. Ad-hoc SQL pasted into a dashboard is how staging and production drift apart, and a multi-tenant schema will change many times before launch. This task also fixes the database conventions every later task relies on, because changing them after 20 migrations is expensive. Docker Desktop is installed; the Supabase CLI is not yet.
ac: Supabase CLI added as a pinned devDependency (npx supabase) so local and CI versions match, and the hosted project linked
supabase/migrations/*.sql is the single source of schema truth
Local Supabase starts via Docker and applies every migration from empty
Naming convention documented in the README
A trivial test migration applies cleanly to a fresh local database
npm scripts exist for db:start, db:reset and db:types (supabase gen types into src/types/database.ts)
Convention documented: any write touching more than one row or table is a Postgres function called via rpc(), because supabase-js has no client-side transactions
Convention documented: views are created WITH (security_invoker = true); SECURITY DEFINER helpers live in a non-exposed schema with a fixed search_path
Local auth emails are captured by the local mail catcher, and email confirmation behaviour is set explicitly in config.toml
out: No production migration runbook yet; that arrives with staging in EP-09.

name: Configure linting, formatting and pre-commit hooks
w: Automatic checks catch type and style errors before they reach a branch, which matters more for a solo developer because there is no reviewer to catch them.
ac: ESLint and Prettier configured with one shared config
npm run lint and npm run format both work
Pre-commit hook runs lint-staged and blocks a failing commit
A deliberate lint error is proven to block a commit
out: No CI pipeline yet (E9-T3). Vitest was added with E1-T10 because the validation layer needed tests.

name: Write setup and run documentation in README
w: A README written while the setup is still fresh is the difference between a recoverable project and a lost weekend. It also becomes the onboarding document for any future collaborator or contractor.
ac: Tool versions and prerequisites documented
Every required environment variable named, with no secret values
Local Supabase start, migrate and seed commands documented
Dev server, lint, typecheck and test commands documented
A fresh clone boots by following only the README
Prerequisites list Node 24 (.nvmrc) and Docker Desktop
out: No architecture decision records in this task.

name: Create Zod validation schema layer
w: Server actions must never trust client input. One reusable validation layer keeps error messages consistent across every form and stops malformed data reaching the database.
ac: Zod schemas exist for hostel, room, resident, allocation and fee inputs
One helper converts a Zod failure into field-level error objects
Server actions return structured field errors instead of raw exceptions
Unit tests cover at least one valid and one invalid case per schema
out: No duplicate validation logic in client components; the same schema is the single source of truth.
